header.name: Attention and perception
header.description:
Attention is one of the major cognitive processes responsible for making us achieve our day-to-day goals. This course-work aims to introduce fundamental principles of how attention helps us to perceive the world around us. Students will be introduced to various experimental paradigms and theories (both classical and contemporary) used to study effects and limitation of attention on human behavior and perception. With the balanced practical sessions and assignments students will develop a fundamental understanding of designing behavioral experiments to study various cognitive processes.
For 500 level, students along with the course work will be additionally required to do a project work involving designing a research experiment, collect and analyse the data along with statistical analysis and has to be submitted in the form of project report & presentation. The research project for 500 level could be either replicating classical experiment/ suggested by the student/ suggested by the course instructor.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to describe fundamental principles of attention and perception.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to explain different behavioural experiments and paradigms used to study the contribution of attention in perception.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to correlate and distinguish putative theories and models of attention.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to explain principle attentional network and neural processes operating in brain.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to design and hypothesize behavioural experiments and analyse the data.

lecture_topics: Selective orientation and shifts of attention
Different types of attention and their role in perception
Cross- modal attention and its perception
